subject: NexusAI: consumption scenarios, $/1M target & peak concurrency
messages:
From: Iris Chan <iris@nexus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Nexus AI Sales <sales@nexus.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: quick numbers from today's discovery

Thanks again for the demo this morning, Jordan — appreciate you walking through Redwood's latency/cost controls. Per our conversation, I'm pulling together the numbers the product team asked for so we can get a baseline pricing conversation started. High-level summary from our side: 

- Expected month 1 (pilot): ~45M tokens/month (mostly outputs from summarization + some embeddings)
- Month 3: ~180M tokens/month (steady ramp as we onboard customers)
- Month 9 (run-rate): planning case ~480M tokens/month; upside scenario 700M tokens/month during product promotions
- Traffic shape: baseline hourly average ~200 TPS equivalent, expected daily peaks to 650 TPS, and rare flash peaks (~1,400 TPS) for ~10–20 minutes during promotions
- Composition: roughly 60% output tokens, 40% input tokens; multi-turn chat sessions are common for 15–30% of sessions
- Target budget: target unit economics are $6–$9 per 1M tokens (we need to stay under $9 in production to meet our gross margin goals)

Can you confirm how Redwood counts tokens (input vs. output) for billing, whether peak bursts are accommodated within hosted slabs or billed as overage, and any recommended slab that fits the above ramp? Attaching our coarse traffic-shape CSV for reference.

Next step we want: a short note of pricing options + recommended slab and expected $/1M for the three ramp points above so we can share internally. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call next week with our platform lead (she's available Tue/Wed AM PT).

Thanks —
Iris Chan
Head of Product Strategy
Nexus AI

Attachment: nexus-traffic-shape.csv (text/csv, 12KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Iris Chan <iris@nexus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: quick numbers from today's discovery

Hi Iris — great summary and thanks for the CSV, that helps a lot. A couple quick clarifications before we pull together a clean pricing view: 

1) Token counting: Redwood's hosted billing separates input vs output for metering but the public unit price is per total input+output tokens. For example, a request with 100 input tokens and 400 output tokens counts as 500 billable tokens. We can show the split in the quote.

2) Bursts vs slabs: For hosted API we recommend a committed monthly slab for predictable unit pricing + an automatic burst buffer. Small, short-duration flash peaks (like the 10–20 minute promos) are usually covered by our burst policy (we keep a short window of reserve throughput). Extended high peaks above the slab will be charged as overage at a higher per-1M rate. For a profile that ramps to 480–700M/mo with 1,400 TPS flashes, a mid-tier slab + burst buffer is the typical fit.

3) Pricing ask: we'll produce three scenario quotes (pilot / ramp / run-rate + upside) with estimated $/1M for each and show the effect of enabling prefix caching and quantization on unit cost. To do that accurately we need two additional items from your side: 
   - Confirm the percent of calls that are single-shot vs multi-turn (you indicated 15–30% multi-turn) — can you provide a rough split as absolute percents?
   - Any regulatory requirements (HIPAA/PHI) or data residency constraints that would push you to Redwood Dedicated/Private?

I've attached a mutual action plan template and will loop in Karthik and Marissa to size pricing bands. Proposed next step: I'll send a formal pricing scenarios email by EOD tomorrow. If you'd rather sync live, Tue 10/14 09:00–09:30 PT works for me.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: mutual-action-plan-template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 48KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: NexusAI: consumption scenarios, $/1M target & peak concurrency

Forwarding Nexus' traffic profile (attached). Key asks: they want three scenario price points (pilot, ramp, run-rate/upside) and to land ~$6–$9 per 1M tokens at run-rate. Traffic notes: 60/40 output/input split, 15–30% multi-turn, daily peaks to ~650 TPS, promotional flash peaks up to ~1,400 TPS for short windows.

Questions for pricing: 
- For our hosted slabs, what's the recommended slab size and list price for each scenario to keep them under $9/1M at run-rate if we enable caching/quantization? Please include the expected effective $/1M assuming: no caching, prefix caching enabled, and prefix+quantization both enabled.
- Any hard limits we should call out for flash peaks (duration we allow before overage kicks in)?

Goal: get a crisp pricing grid + recommended SLA/burst policy by EOD tomorrow so I can send it to Iris ahead of the Tue call.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: NexusAI: consumption scenarios, $/1M target & peak concurrency

Quick initial grid attached. Early takeaways: 

- Pilot (45M/mo): recommend Small slab at list $14/1M, discounted to $10/1M if they commit 3-month pilot paid upfront; with prefix caching expect effective $8–9/1M
- Ramp (180M/mo): Medium slab, list $12/1M, discounted to $8/1M with a 6-month commit; caching + quantization could push effective to ~$6.2/1M
- Run-rate (480M–700M/mo): Large slab, list $10/1M, volume-discount to $6.5/1M with 12-month commit + standard caching; aggressive quantization plus dedicated caching could go to ~$5.5/1M but adds quality/regression risk that must be evaluated

Burst policy proposal: allow 15-minute sustained bursts at up to 2x slab throughput in hosted with soft throttling; anything above that triggers overage. Flash peaks (1,400 TPS for 10–20 minutes) would be covered within the 15-minute burst buffer for the Medium->Large slab sizes; if Nexus wants guaranteed no-throttle for promos we should propose Dedicated or a higher reserved slab.

I'll attach the rough-pricing-grid.xlsx with the numbers. Jordan — if you want, I can convert this into the three-scenario quote and include a recommended contract language blurb for burst handling.

-Karthik
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rough-pricing-grid.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 22KB)
